entries.title: After Enter, Backspace, Delete, Tab, Shift+Tab or a multi-block paste in a long windowed page the caret stays on screen and the view moves only as far as showing it needs (a Backspace merge into a tall image block no longer leaves the caret scrolled out above the viewport or throws the view up by most of a screen)
entries.notes: REOPENED 2026-10-23: Beta 9 still jumps on level 2 to 1 Shift+Tab and Tab back to 2 (Windows 10, WebView2 153); prior fix evidence revoked for this outcome. GH #745 (Windows 10 Beta 7 and a laptop on Beta 6: the view jumps after Enter or Backspace on a long page, 'seems to need images above'). Not a 0.8 regression: origin/master 2d0cb1f07 and release/0.8 582e27dff behave identically. Root cause: the caret moves into another block editor at mount via textarea.focus() (Block.tsx focusNow), whose native scroll is engine-specific: Chromium/WebView2 centres the field, WebKitGTK does not scroll. A Backspace merge into a block whose rendered image makes it hundreds of px taller than its raw-text editor puts the merged caret row far outside the viewport. Fail-before on the Beta 7 binary (582e27dff), WebKitGTK, scripts/e2e-gh745-structural-edit-viewport.mjs: backspace-into-image caretTop -477 (editor top -505, scrollTop unchanged); in a Chromium harness the same merge moves scrollTop by -690. Same fail-before in the right sidebar (caretTop -182, scrollTop unchanged) and on a nested page with a sticky parent pin (caretTop -454). Fix: the editor focuses with preventScroll and src/editor/caretReveal.ts reveals the caret row by the least scroll once the layout has been still for two frames (revealing at mount measured a transient remount layout 6000px off), below the shown pins. The Enter-only symptom of the Windows report did not reproduce on Linux WebKitGTK or in the Chromium harness, with or without images.

entries.title: Sticky ancestors keep the next readable child visible while scrolling nested outlines without moving document content
entries.notes: Real browser geometry at depths 2–4, short/long branches, single/multiline parents, desktop and phone widths; parents activate at the bottom of their sticky slot before the next child enters it. See RECEIPT-fix-sticky-overlap.md for evidence and platform limits. REOPENED 2026-10-19 and fixed on batch/fix-sticky-subtree (EllisMorrow, #717 comment 3, Beta 5 still wrong): a pin must stay inside its own subtree: sticky 1a (child 1aa) in `0 > 1 > 1a > 1aa; 2 > 2a; 3` covered the next row `2`, and in `0 > 1 > (1a > 1aa), 1b, 1c, 1d; 2; 3` covered its sibling `1b`; a block at the same level or higher must push the pin up and out, never be covered by it. The reporter's outlines are in scripts/shot-sticky-overlap.mjs (subtree phase: no pin overlaps a row outside its own subtree at nesting depths 2-5, desktop and phone widths, pane and sidebar, zoom 1.25, single and multi-line parents; the next row pushes the pin up and out; layout identical with and without pins). Cause: the pin margin-bottom:-30px made its sticky margin box zero-high, so it could hang 30 px below its own block; it now keeps its 30 px in flow and the row pulls itself up with margin-top:-30px. Not verified on Windows or an Android device.

entries.title: Repeated collapse of a block whose collapsed:: row trails its quote keeps one hidden row instead of stacking visible text

Fix: block regions own trailing built-in rows (collapsed, logseq.order-list-type; not id, which lsdoc folds only when uppercase and its facets would not see) of a final quote, and the wasm render AST drops them. Any real text edit of such a block also moves the claimed rows before the quote (joinProps #684 placement; harmless). Platform-independent (reproduced in jsdom on release/0.8); native journey is the Linux control. Load-time collapsed state follows mldoc and OG (a swallowed row does not load as collapsed); the first collapse therefore moves the row before the quote (UI-GH721-QUOTE-TRAILER-COLLAPSE-PERSISTS).

Fix: new pure refCompletionEnd(value,end,insertedText) in autocomplete.ts scans forward on the CURRENT LINE for the closer matching the completion's suffix (]]/))/}}), returning just past it or the caret when none ahead; replaceTrigger now uses it. Covers page AND block refs (same latent defect) and the latent end-caret ]]]] doubling. Not a regression: latent since the autocomplete feature shipped (e54ad36e, 2026-06-14). entries.title: YouTube video macros initialize without configuration error 153 in native Linux WebViews
entries.notes: Blocking core operation. Real Tauri/WebKitGTK 2.50.6 custom-protocol base produces error 153 with the reported video. Shared reader reports position to pane/session; first annotation retains guarded paired publication. entries.title: A shutdown, logout, closed terminal or Ctrl+C (SIGTERM, SIGHUP, SIGINT) ends Tine through its normal Quit within a bound, so the next launch does not report an unclean exit

coverage.scenario: SIGTERM and SIGHUP to the app alone: the app exits, an edit typed within the save debounce is on disk and diagnostics/session-active is gone; SIGTERM then SIGHUP, and SIGINT, to the app and all its WebKit helpers at once (a session stop, a terminal's process group): the app exits within 30 s and the marker is gone

entries.notes: GH #701 (Dieterbe: the 'did not close cleanly' notice after every launch, because the computer is shut down with Tine open). The default signal action ended the process at once (exit 143): RunEvent::Exit never ran, so the ADR 0058 marker stayed and an edit typed within the save debounce was lost. Fail-before on the deployed 0.8.0-beta.1 binary: the journey's typed edit was not on disk. Windows sign-out already exits through WM_ENDSESSION (GH #455); mobile follows visibility. Review round 1 (Opus/medium adversarial): a session stop or process-group signal kills WebKit's helpers too, so the close request was never answered and the first fix hung with the marker; systemd's SIGHUP after SIGTERM was treated as 'asked twice' and exited at once. Fix round 2: later signals are ignored and after 5 s the graph windows are destroyed, exiting through the retirement waiter (G6). The journey now signals the whole process tree.

entries.title: A table block that is the first bullet of a page with no page properties is not rewritten as page properties, so typing its title or rows never raises the page-header toast or stops the page saving; a real invalid header toast names its first bad line and is not stacked
entries.notes: Dieterbe (0.8.0-beta.3) saw the toast with a x2 badge on a journal with no page properties; the top of the page was a table block (tine.view:: table, tine.table-widths::) with rows. Root cause: a title-less first bullet carrying only tine.* config is a promotable page header (childless, properties-only), so the first save folded it into the preamble and adoptFoldedPageHeader marked the live block as the header; its title and rows then made an invalid header draft that pageToDto refused to save, with the toast on every exit. Fixed like GH #540: tine.view and the rest of the block-only tine.* view/sheet config keys (tine.table-widths, tine.col-widths, tine.group-by, tine.sort, ... but NOT the page-level schema keys tine.fields/tine.type/tine.tag-table) are block-scoped keys (Rust and TS lists, kept equal by i12PageHeader.test.ts), so Show children as: Outline, which removes only tine.view, leaves a block. Intentional difference from OG: OG never authors tine.view; Martin, D-20261018-H210. One predicate (TS isPropertiesOnly, Rust is_page_header_candidate) decides header-or-block for display, edits, page-property writes (alias/icon/filters never land in a table block), alias reading and save-time promotion. Also: the toast only fires while the marked node is the page's first root (a node pushed below another block is no longer the header; the store refuses to save that page: refusing to move page-header property into outline content, GH #163 firewall, follow-up F1), is ONE toast per page (replaced when the text changes, dismissed when the header is valid again or no longer first), and names the bad line / child blocks. Fail-before: the render journey and the Rust test fail on 4e389bcfe (pre_block 'tine.view:: table...' written to the file); the B1 (alias/icon/filters into the table block, alias::-spelling in query.rs) and R1 (Outline leaving tine.table-widths) tests fail without the shared predicate. The double toast was not reproduced as a single exit raising it twice (jsdom raises no blur on editor removal); it is two exits stacking into the x2 badge, which is now one toast. Windows/macOS/Android unverified; the real-app journey is scripts/e2e-page-properties.mjs (GH #210 section; it types the title on its own line above the config, as the reporter did).

entries.title: Cutting a block in query results deleted the query: a right click on a query result (or a block inside an embed) must open that block's own menu, never the host block's, so Cut/Delete act on the result on its own page
entries.notes: Reported on 0.8.0-beta.5 Linux with {{tine-query ...}} results. OG og-1.0.0 frontend/components/content.cljs hiccup-content resolves the block menu from the nearest .bullet-container[blockid] and cuts that block (editor-handler/cut-block!). Root cause: Block.tsx block-main onContextMenu never stopped propagation, so the host row's handler ran after the nested result row's and its openContextMenu(host) won; unloaded result stand-ins and legacy query-table cells had no handler and fell through to the host. Fix: the nearest block row owns the menu (contextMenuPolicy ownsBlockContextMenu) and the query results region is a data-block-surface. A transparent whole-block embed's root row still opens the embed occurrence's menu (as its drag, master GH #514). Fail-before: jsdom suite (9 of 17 fail on pre-fix code; the 8 others guard already-correct paths: table-view rows, keyboard Delete/Backspace/Mod+X and Backspace-merge, host bullet, embed root) and the native journey on the deployed pre-fix Beta binary removed the query line from Queries___TasksUnscheduled.md. entries.title: On phones and tablets, which have no tab strip, no menu offers Open in new tab and no modified click or Search chord opens a background tab the user cannot reach
Pressing Enter at the start of a page's properties never stops the page saving: the properties stay the page header and later edits on that page still save
entries.notes: GH #210 review r1 F1 (card Bqx04). Fixed per D-20261019-H210F1 (do what OG does: OG 6e7afa8eb editor.cljs keydown-new-block -> dwim-in-properties inserts a newline on a property line, and wrap-parse-block string/triml drops a leading blank line at save). Now a header draft is canonicalized (leading blank lines and trailing newlines dropped) for validity, fold and property rows; the kernel turns a split at the head or inside the first-root page header into a newline in it, and refuses (Reason::HeaderRoot) any verb that leaves the header no longer roots[0] (move up/drop/insert above it); the store firewall is unchanged. Intentional differences: on a non-property line of a header draft Enter is a newline (OG splits); moves above the header are refused (OG would demote the properties). Fail-before: 8/12 unit, 4/4 render, 4 kernel tests, and the native journey against the og binary (body edit never reached disk). A page stuck by an older build recovers by deleting the empty first block. Reproduced on og 2195632b6: click the page-properties header, caret to offset 0, Enter. The header textarea's Enter-on-a-property-line branch inserts a newline, so the header draft starts with a blank line; pageHeaderDraftProblem calls that invalid, pageToDto returns null and the page never saves again. A split that reaches the outline kernel (any caller of splitBlock) instead puts an empty block above the header, which the store refuses (GH #163 firewall: refusing to move page-header property into outline content).

Backport of og 007cbc245 to release/0.8 (D-20261020-CC10): release/0.8 has one template walk (tine-store query::templates, which also serves the new-journal template), so the header check lives there; og's tine-core template.rs and the file-scoped daily-template lookup do not exist on this line. entries.title: Typing DOING keeps the caret on the task line after the auto-written clock-in, clocks in once, and a CLOCK line that is not in a recognised drawer renders instead of blanking the page
entries.notes: GH #741 (Windows, 0.8.0-beta.6; reproduces on stable 0.7.4 code and release/0.8). Typing DOING made the live-mirrored commit append the :LOGBOOK: clock-in, the textarea re-synced and the browser put the caret at the end, so the title text landed after :END:. The parser reads that CLOCK line as a paragraph inline (ts Clock, date a [Started|Stopped, value] pair), and timestampText read date.year off the pair and threw, which the page-level FailureBoundary turned into 'This page could not be displayed' (Retry re-throws) until the block was fixed in another editor. Fixes: timestampText handles Clock and renders any unknown shape as empty text (OG block.cljs inline Timestamp falls to ""); commit() maps the caret through a programmatic rewrite (OG never rewrites the buffer while editing; OG also hides the logbook from the edit buffer, which Tine still shows: follow-up); the previous marker for the transition is read off the title line, else the next keystroke clocked in a second time. Fail-before on release/0.8 582e27dff: 16 of 17 unit cases red, and the native journey (Linux WebKitGTK, debug build): typed text lands after :END: ('DOING\n:LOGBOOK:...:END: test', caret at the end), and each damaged page (text after :END:, backtick after :END:) shows 'This page could not be displayed. undefined is not an object (evaluating t.year)' and the quick switcher then cannot open any other page.

entries.title: Holding a key on a large graph no longer makes typing stall more and more: while the backlinks, unlinked references, page icons, block refs and queries are still refreshing after one save, the next saves wait for that refresh and then refresh once, with the latest text
entries.notes: Related to GH #746 (periodic typing freeze on a large graph, Windows, Beta); not proven to be its cause. Since 0.8.0-beta.1 the page is sent about once per second while typing (318a6f40a) and 700 ms after each publication wiring.ts notePublication bumped dataRev with no in-flight guard; every dataRev reader refetches whole-graph reads that run on the host blocking pool and are never cancelled. When one refresh round costs more than about 1 s the rounds overlap and pile up (reads in flight 6 -> 49-59 in 20 s on hosted Windows, input gaps 212 -> 374 ms, under an artificial per-read CPU cost). Fix: the save-driven bump waits until no refresh read is in flight (REFRESH_HOLD_MAX_MS = 5 s at most), and publications meanwhile coalesce into one trailing bump after the last of them. Fail-before on release/0.8 cd7961e81 wiring.ts: 4 of 5 wiring.refreshGuard cases red (three publications during one slow round gave 3 rounds instead of 1).

entries.title: Typing on a page whose linked or unlinked references are large stays smooth: the refresh after each save keeps the shown answer (no Loading flash), rebuilds the reference filter index only while a filter or search is in use, and does not remount rows whose content did not change
entries.notes: GH #746 (Windows, 0.8.0-beta.8; smooth on stable 0.7.4). The reporter's DevTools trace: every ~1.8 s while a key is held, a ~100 ms renderer task receiving a 13 MB IPC answer (the page's unlinked references), then a ~710 ms microtask run. Source-mapped against a byte-identical rebuild of beta.8 (app-Dnjzxfpl.js): 84% of the 710 ms is LinkedReferences.tsx fallbackByRoot (fallbackFilterEntry -> searchFold -> wasm search_fold over every reference root and its subtree), the rest the coRefs chip memo (navigationName/pageIdentityKey per facet). Both are eager Solid memos over the whole answer, so they ran after every refetch even with the section collapsed and no filter open; 0.7.4 did not refetch references while typing (93265bc01, GH #659/#660, made them refetch per save). Fix: the index and chips are built only while the filter panel is open or a filter/search is active; the unlinked header shows Loading only before the first answer; LiveRefGroup keeps the previous DTO/evidence object when its content is unchanged (not for query rows, whose objects carry a results ticket), so excerpt and DTO rows are not remounted. Also: the GH #746 refresh guard now counts block_referrers, get_backlink_filter_context, page_backlink_counts and page_modified. Fail-before on release/0.8 56bd13337: 240 search folds over 3 refreshes (expected 0), Loading during a refresh, and the unchanged row remounted; refresh-guard test: 0 of 4 new reads counted.

entries.title: Opening a PDF at a saved zoom does not later pull the reader to the top of the page, over the backlink's highlight or over the reader's own scrolling
entries.notes: The saved or fit scale is applied before the page layout exists; that write armed the 120 ms zoom-settle timer, whose page-top anchor restore then ran 120 ms after the mount: over the exact-highlight scroll of a backlink followed just after opening, or over the next user scroll (the rare 'page input 1' flake of the GH #672 journey, Windows run 39345257095 and a local Linux release run). Component probe (two cases) failed before (scrollTop 80, expected 514 / 1086) and passes after. Native: the probe trace of the pre-fix binary showed set 80 from the settle 19 ms after the second backlink landed; the journey now also asserts the landed highlight stays in view for 600 ms. The native assertion only catches the race when the harness clicks within ~120 ms of the mount; the component probe is the deterministic proof.

entries.title: A backlink or block reference to a highlight of a PDF that is not open yet scrolls to that highlight, not just marks it
entries.notes: Card hCAoxs (found by the GH #672 lane). Opening the reader for a reference called renderPage(target page) and centred the highlight after the await; the IntersectionObserver's request for the same page supersedes that raster, so the await returned before the overlay was painted and the centre-scroll was skipped (the highlight was marked but left off-screen; OG scrolls to it). The scroll is now owed as a pending target applied by whichever raster of the page completes at the current scale (not while a zoom is settling, once, cancelled by the reader's wheel/mouse/touch). Component tests (pages 1 and 3) failed before (no scrollIntoView on the highlight) and pass after; the wheel-cancel case guards the new mechanism. Journey: the cold-open block reference of PDF B must land its highlight inside the scroller and keep it there for 600 ms.

entries.title: Clicking a hidden {{cloze}} reveals the answer in place instead of opening the block editor
entries.notes: GH #763. The cloze toggles on click, but the press entered the block editor on mousedown first (the .cloze span was not in FORBID_EDIT_SELECTOR), which unmounted the cloze before its click. OG renders the cloze as an <a> (srs.cljs), which its target-forbidden-edit? already skips; .cloze is now on Tine's list, shared by blocks, Rendered, tables and grids.
